subject.title: fix(memory-wiki): reject oversized apply body files

question: Should `wiki apply synthesis --body-file` adopt a hard 1 MiB maximum for existing users, or should the memory-safety work preserve support for larger regular files until a separately approved limit exists?
rationale: This is a user-visible compatibility change to an established CLI option, and the supplied discussion contains no maintainer-approved size contract or upgrade policy.

options.title: Preserve existing input compatibility
options.body: Remove the unconditional 1 MiB rejection and pursue bounded-memory protection without silently narrowing accepted regular-file inputs.

options.title: Adopt a documented 1 MiB contract
options.body: Approve the limit explicitly, document the user-visible behavior and error, and require current-head validation around the boundary before merge.

recommendation.title: Preserve existing input compatibility
recommendation.body: Remove the unconditional 1 MiB rejection and pursue bounded-memory protection without silently narrowing accepted regular-file inputs.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR timeline explicitly routes review attention to steipete, and the unresolved question is product-contract direction rather than a mechanical test repair.
